steps.title: Open the live tape cockpit
steps.narration: Tapeology opens to a single live cockpit that watches one stock at a time. Before you pick a stock it sits quietly at idle, with no invented numbers, just a prompt to start watching.
steps.point_out: The ticker box and green Watch button in the header, the 'idle' status in the top-right, and the empty 'No ticker watched' state.

steps.title: Enter the down-tape sample stock
steps.narration: Let's start with the brand-new ability this round adds: reading a market where sellers are in charge. Type the built-in down-tape sample, SIM-SELLER, into the ticker box.
steps.point_out: SIM-SELLER typed into the ticker box, ready to watch.

steps.title: Sellers in control, shown in rose
steps.narration: Click Watch and the cockpit fills itself live and settles on 'Seller Control' — the first time the product reads a down-tape. It only makes this call because aggressive selling is genuinely pushing the price down, not merely because sell volume is high.
steps.point_out: The rose 'Seller Control' headline with high confidence, a high Aggressive sell ratio, a negative Sell price impact, the three seller observations, and 'Tape state changed to seller_control' in the Event Log.

steps.title: Back to a fresh cockpit
steps.narration: Now let's confirm the older up-tape reading still works exactly as before. We reload to a clean cockpit first.
steps.point_out: The cockpit returns to its empty 'No ticker watched' state, ready for the next stock.

steps.title: Enter the up-tape sample stock
steps.narration: This time we'll watch the up-tape sample, SIM-BUYER, where aggressive buyers are lifting the price.
steps.point_out: SIM-BUYER typed into the ticker box.

steps.title: Buyers in control, still shown in green
steps.narration: Click Watch and the cockpit settles on 'Buyer Control' in green — the up-tape reading is untouched by the new seller logic. The same screen now speaks both directions in its own color: rose for sellers, green for buyers.
steps.point_out: The green 'Buyer Control' headline, a positive Buy price impact, and 'Tape state changed to buyer_control' in the Event Log — the buyer read is intact.

steps.title: Back to a fresh cockpit
steps.narration: One last check — the product's honesty promise. Let's reset and try a stock the system doesn't recognise.

steps.title: Enter an unknown ticker
steps.narration: Type a made-up ticker, NOPE123, that isn't one of the built-in sample stocks.
steps.point_out: NOPE123 entered in the ticker box.

steps.title: Unknown stocks are refused, never faked
steps.narration: Click Watch and the cockpit refuses politely: it shows a clear error and reads nothing at all, rather than inventing a fake tape state to look busy. No data is ever fabricated.
steps.point_out: The rose error line under the header and the cockpit staying empty — no made-up 'control' reading for a stock it doesn't know.

expect.text: is not a known simulated ticker
